I have resolved the issue where email messages crash with a `UnicodeEncodeError` when the domain/hostname contains non-ASCII characters and the email encoding is non-Unicode (such as `iso-8859-1`).

### Summary of Changes
- Added a [`punycode()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/utils/encoding.py#L251-L253) helper in [encoding.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/utils/encoding.py) to convert non-ASCII domain names to Punycode (`domain.encode('idna').decode('ascii')`).
- Updated [`CachedDnsName.get_fqdn()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/mail/utils.py#L16-L19) in [utils.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/mail/utils.py) and [`EmailMessage.message()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/mail/message.py#L255-L257) in [message.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/mail/message.py) (as well as [`sanitize_address()`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/mail/message.py#L74-L108), [validators.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/core/validators.py), and [html.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-k4kb1zdy/django/utils/html.py)) to convert domains to Punycode.
